line.text: '* Avoid deploying any unnecessary Jump Beacons. On the higher difficulty levels, their maintenance cost is very high.'
'* The "Dry dock" perk lowers maintenance of docked Capital ships by 75% and smaller ships by 25%.'
'* Ship Quality directly affects maintenance costs. It can nearly double for the lowest quality ships!'
'* "Advanced ships" are 35% more expensive to maintain.'
'* With the exception of Private Corp. ships, Phanon ships (requires main plot completion), and Yaki ships (if you have infamy), all ships not made by your origin faction cost 35% more maintenance.'
' * If you started as a Xenon Defect, Phanon ships are always exempt from this penalty, while OCV ships cost 15% more maintenance instead of 35%.'
'* For ships produced at Outposts with the "Advanced engineering" perk, maintenance costs are reduced by 50%.'
'* Maintenance costs rise sharply when fleet supply usage exceeds capacity. Expanding supply capacity or reducing fleet size can quickly stabilize your economy.'
'* Build your own Advanced Satellite Factory and base some fast M5 fighters there. You can then set them as Automated explorers. This also works from Outposts.'
'* Automated explorers have a 15-jump range from their home base.'
'* Explorers based at the same station will always explore different sectors without overlap.'
'* Good to Know: NPC explorers on harder difficulties have the ability to claim sectors.'
'* Explorers will avoid Blacklisted sectors. You may have to explore those personally.'
'* On harder difficulties, other factions will periodically "clean out" some of your satellites, so your automated explorers will stay very busy replacing them.'

'* Capital ships do not do very well at docking or traversing through gates when you are in-sector with them. They tend to clog up because of their collision avoidance which is active only when you are present in the sector.'
' * If you want them to move without clogging up, be somewhere else. They move normally within the sector while you are there.'

'* If you are in-sector with your fleet, all damage (from all sides) is greatly magnified, so if you want a fight over quickly, be there in that sector. Out-of-sector, all damage is reduced to about 1/3.'

'* Chaff is not considered for OOS battles, so if you are never where the fighting is, do not bother with it. OOS battles are simulated and use a simplified calculation which does not consider all factors.'
'* Use colored crystals to upgrade your ships in the Outpost Hangar. In particular, the CCDS1/2/3 allow chaff to repel the 3 missile types in the game.'

'* The Jump station perk is limited, so use it in critical areas where you may get attacked and cannot risk relying on fragile Jump Beacons. Losing your Jump Beacon when trying to respond to an attack will ruin your day.'

'* Remember that you cannot place beacons in sectors you do not own on Hard and Insane difficulties, unless you are close allies with the sector's owner or the sector is abandoned. This makes expansion far more difficult and mirrors NPC limitations.'

'* NPC factions will sometimes send in small raiding strikes deep into your territory during wartime. These are small fleets of fast fighters that will kill your Outpost Agents and Traders, so protect the homeland.'
'* Recycling a ship adds its crew to the Outpost's population and partially refunds the ship's construction materials.'

'* Your total supply is determined based on your global maximum population. If your current supply exceeds your total supply, you can increase your total supply by terraforming planets or placing Outposts in newly conquered sectors.'
' * Alternatively, you can reduce your current supply by retiring or losing ships, either via recycling or destruction.'
'* The "Faster research" Perk greatly improves all research in that sector.'
'* Researching ships of your origin faction gives a large bonus.'
'* Researching ships from factions that border your sector gives you a bonus.'
'* A Research Favor from another faction can temporarily improve your research rate.'
'* Being in a Coalition can improve your research rate.'
'* OCV ship research is improved in sectors with stronger abnormal signals.'
'* Yaki ship research is improved if you have infamy.'
'* Terran ships can be researched only in sectors with Terran Memory.'
'* You can use your Data Scanner to scan your own ships whose blueprints you have not yet unlocked.'

'* If you cannot catch someone, you cannot kill them. Speed kills. For example, the Split have the fastest ships, but they are somewhat weak in defenses. Used properly, they can be deadly. Each faction has its own particular advantages to learn and exploit.'
'* Escort your large capital ships with some M6s. These provide good anti-fighter defense and they can hold up in a heavy fight.'

'* Create fast raiding fleets of M3s. In the Fleet Settings screen, set them to attack only enemy freighters and patrol an enemy faction's space. They will quickly decimate enemy haulers while running from other fights. This can devastate the economy of an opponent.'

'* Missiles in Renegades have greatly enhanced damage. They are expensive but deal more damage than in any prior versions of X3 mods. M7Ms are very effective long-range anti-capital forces, and M8s can be devastating against fighters.'

'* Grouping your forces is essential to surviving large engagements. Streaming in your attack ships one by one is the best way to lose them. When invading a sector, consider first sending in one or two fast fighters and directing them to the far side of the target sector. When the defenses move far from your gate to engage those fighters, stream in your large ships.'

'* For large capital ship engagements in-sector, use fast, nimble fighters to draw fire from enemy capital ships and away from your capital ships. These force the enemy to waste their high-damage weapons on nimble, hard-to-hit ships.'
'* Be sure to set up a Supplier in the Fleet Settings screen to automatically restore your missile reserves.'
'* Moving capital ships through gates is vastly slower with the player in-sector. If you need to get them through a gate fast, be somewhere else.'

'* In sectors that don't have a Jump Beacon, use only local Agents to import from and export to local factories, then set other Agents to move full loads between other Outposts. This maximizes the inter-sector loads you carry and is the key to efficiency.'
'* In general, an Agent can support up to 3-4 factories. For example, sectors with 15 factories may need 3-4 Agents.'
'* A Courier is more efficient than an Agent when transferring multiple wares between Outposts.'

'* Outpost Traders are used for buying materials from NPCs or selling excess items to NPCs. When neither is needed, they start trading between NPCs for pure profit, so they can be a huge source of income over time. Any successful trade with an NPC improves your reputation with its faction.'
'* If you can afford the maintenance costs, research a fast TS-class ship to use as your Agents. The faster resources are moved around your empire, the smoother it will run.'
'* If you find your Agents doing nothing most of the time, assign them to do something else. Optimize the use of your Agents to keep costs down.'

'* Review the "Logistics" screen in your Personal Console. This summarizes the total empire production and consumption, showing you exactly when you need more or fewer factories. It is critical to check on your logistics as you expand your empire.'

'* The default station trade range limit in Mayhem 3 is 8 jumps (does not include Jump Points). Your Agents will limit themselves to this range if their Outpost jump range is greater. If you raise it, the demand on your CPU can rise dramatically, so keep an eye out for this.'

'* Your logistics ships will need maintenance once in a while. Be sure to review your Maintenance screen in your Personal Console and occasionally send them for inspection. Otherwise their maintenance will be very high.'

line.text: '* Use Private Corp. ships to fill gaps in your fleet. They are flexible, but specialized faction ships perform better in combat.'
' * For example, the Truelight Seeker excels at repairs but is less effective in combat.'
' * The Aran serves as a mobile base, repairing ships 4x faster than standard carriers, but cannot fight.'
'* Do not undervalue mining ships. While mining ore and silicon, they also collect colored crystals which are used for ship upgrades and as commodities at trade stations.'
'* When at war, consider placing a few picket ships out 2 or 3 jumps from your main hubs. This can be an essential early warning system if you get too busy micromanaging.'

'* The chances that NPC factions will declare war on you increase if you have infamy, have a negative reputation with them, hold a de jure sector, or have a low "Total Ship Power to Sector Count ratio."'
'* On harder difficulties and fighting far from home, consider loading a cheap factory and a Jump Beacon on one of your capital ships, assuming you have one with the necessary cargo space.'

' * In a pinch, you can run to an unclaimed sector and then drop the Jump Beacon, allowing you to escape. Dropping the factory prevents other factions from simply conquering that sector, thus ensuring your Jump Beacon stays.'

line.text: '* Generally, a faction must share a border with you in order to declare war on you. Higher difficulties increase the chance of going to war.'

'* Depending on how much progress you have towards a ship blueprint, recycling a ship will give anywhere between 10-40% of its blueprint, up until 85% (50% for advanced ships, 70% for prototype ships). The remainder must be completed by research or via the Data Scanner.'

'* Different factions have different ship advantages and loadouts. For example, the Split have the fastest ships, Teladi have the largest cargo bays, Boron have Ion weapons, and Terran have the most powerful weapons. Each faction has its own disadvantages as well.'
'* Renegade ships move faster when they start fleeing to a station.'

'* All ships you own consume supply. Monitor your supply usage carefully: exceeding capacity will not only increase ship construction and maintenance costs but also cause other factions to increase their vigilance.'
'* Fleet members can get dispersed during combat operations. You can periodically regroup them by issuing the "Followers: Join with Commander" command.'

'* If you want your fleets to focus their fire on one target at a time, set their scanning range to 0 km, and set "Followers engage commander's target" to YES. It can be less efficient, but you will lose fewer ships.'

'* You can assign an automated Missile Supplier that will top up all your ships in the field. Upgrade a TS hauler with a Transporter Device and position it out in space. In the Fleet Settings screen, select "Supplier:" and choose this hauler.'

'* A Supplier will retrieve missiles from its homebase or request that its homebase build more as needed. It automatically restocks your ships. Set your ship restock amounts at the bottom of the "Advanced/Weapons..." menu for that ship.'
'* This screen shows the slowest ship in the fleet. This is important because a fleet travels at the pace of its slowest member.'
'* For fast raiding fleets composed of fighters, it is useful to select the option to "Ignore Big and Huge Ships".'
'* Fleets can automatically reinforce themselves by setting the "Build Followers" menu. This is limited to only one type of ship, but it can be useful for homogeneous fleets.'
'* Port research takes time and money. A higher research rate will improve your port research time.'
'* Oxygen and accounting hacks take the longest to complete.'
'* The "Hacking Station" perk is required to convert a research station into a hacking station.'
'* Good Hacking Station locations cover a lot of nearby sectors. Place them as close to the targets as possible.'

'* There is a tradeoff between efficiency and security. Higher efficiency increases the jump range of your virus but decreases security. Decreased security increases the chance of being backtraced (victims may try to counter-hack your ships in response).'
'* Advanced Firewall Software protects your ships against counter-hacks. All your ships can be counter-hacked.'
'* Expect losses. You may lose additional men after you gain control of the boarded ship. The fewer marines left when the operation completes, the fewer additional men you will lose.'
'* For tougher targets, reinforce your boarding party by sending in additional marines.'

'* In general, new marines need to go through at least one deck's worth of time in order to reinforce your surviving marines. They need more time the farther you are from your target when you launch Boarding Pods.'
'* Boarding can net you a lot of resources, but it is generally frowned upon and also has its own set of risks.'
'* Boarding abandoned ships results in significantly fewer losses than boarding manned ships.'
'* Shield Hack and EMP can be used as alternatives to keep your target's shields down.'
'* Boarding a ship yields up to the first 25% of a ship blueprint and some valuables.'
'* Roaming Renegade ships are most valuable when captured intentionally rather than destroyed.'
'* Boarded ships retain any existing Pandora Tunings.'
'* Xenon ships are extremely difficult to board. Those recovered intact may offer benefits that destruction never provides.'
' * Some commanders believe capturing Xenon capital ships earns goodwill across the galaxy, but few live to confirm it.'
'* As you progress through the main plot, you can choose to continue helping Phanon or to progress through the Synthetic Dawn Plot and join the OCV. Each route has its advantages.'
'* The main plot normally starts when you have established an empire, but the alternate route can be started as soon as you place your first Outpost.'
'* When the Phanon arrive, they will need your help. Speed up their growth by selling shipbuilding materials to them.'
'* Terraforming a planet in one of your sectors will penalize not only the production rates at the local Outpost but also at other Outposts.'

'* Hacking, ship extensions, and maintenance are free if you join the OCV. You get other benefits, such as improved recruited marines and no food consumption by default. However, this comes at a great cost...'

'* OCV ships are cheaper and stronger than even Terran ships, but all your OCV ships will eventually turn to OCV control. The time it takes to convert is determined by the abnormal signal strength of the sector where they were built or captured and by ship quality.'

'* Higher abnormal signals and lower ship quality will shorten the timer before OCV ships join the OCV faction. On the plus side, OCV ships build faster and are cheaper to build in sectors with higher abnormal signal strength.'
'* Lower abnormal signals and higher ship quality will lengthen the timer before OCV ships join the OCV faction.'
'* Researching OCV ships in a sector with 0% abnormal signal strength is significantly slower than researching OCV ships in a sector with at least 1% abnormal signal strength.'

sval.val: --- Maintenance Tips ---
* Avoid deploying any unnecessary Jump Beacons. On the higher difficulty levels, their maintenance cost is very high.
* The "Dry dock" perk lowers maintenance of docked Capital ships by 75% and smaller ships by 25%.
* Ship Quality directly affects maintenance costs. It can nearly double for the lowest quality ships!
* "Advanced ships" are 35% more expensive to maintain.
* With the exception of Private Corp. ships, Phanon ships (requires main plot completion), and Yaki ships (if you have infamy), all ships not made by your origin faction cost 35% more maintenance.
* If you started as a Xenon Defect, Phanon ships are always exempt from this penalty, while OCV ships cost 15% more maintenance instead of 35%.
* For ships produced at Outposts with the "Advanced engineering" perk, maintenance costs are reduced by 50%.
* Maintenance costs rise sharply when fleet supply usage exceeds capacity. Expanding supply capacity or reducing fleet size can quickly stabilize your economy.
--- Automated Exploration Tips ---

* Automated explorers have a 15-jump range from their home base.
* Explorers based at the same station will always explore different sectors without overlap.
* Good to Know: NPC explorers on harder difficulties have the ability to claim sectors.
* Explorers will avoid Blacklisted sectors. You may have to explore those personally.
* On harder difficulties, other factions will periodically "clean out" some of your satellites, so your automated explorers will stay very busy replacing them.
--- Random Tips ---

* Capital ships do not do very well at docking or traversing through gates when you are in-sector with them. They tend to clog up because of their collision avoidance which is active only when you are present in the sector.
* If you want them to move without clogging up, be somewhere else. They move normally within the sector while you are there.

* If you are in-sector with your fleet, all damage (from all sides) is greatly magnified, so if you want a fight over quickly, be there in that sector. Out-of-sector, all damage is reduced to about 1/3.

* Chaff is not considered for OOS battles, so if you are never where the fighting is, do not bother with it. OOS battles are simulated and use a simplified calculation which does not consider all factors.
* Use colored crystals to upgrade your ships in the Outpost Hangar. In particular, the CCDS1/2/3 allow chaff to repel the 3 missile types in the game.

* The Jump station perk is limited, so use it in critical areas where you may get attacked and cannot risk relying on fragile Jump Beacons. Losing your Jump Beacon when trying to respond to an attack will ruin your day.

* Remember that you cannot place beacons in sectors you do not own on Hard and Insane difficulties, unless you are close allies with the sector's owner or the sector is abandoned. This makes expansion far more difficult and mirrors NPC limitations.

* NPC factions will sometimes send in small raiding strikes deep into your territory during wartime. These are small fleets of fast fighters that will kill your Outpost Agents and Traders, so protect the homeland.
* Recycling a ship adds its crew to the Outpost's population and partially refunds the ship's construction materials.

* Your total supply is determined based on your global maximum population. If your current supply exceeds your total supply, you can increase your total supply by terraforming planets or placing Outposts in newly conquered sectors.
* Alternatively, you can reduce your current supply by retiring or losing ships, either via recycling or destruction.
--- Research Tips ---
* The "Faster research" Perk greatly improves all research in that sector.
* Researching ships of your origin faction gives a large bonus.
* Researching ships from factions that border your sector gives you a bonus.
* A Research Favor from another faction can temporarily improve your research rate.
* Being in a Coalition can improve your research rate.
* OCV ship research is improved in sectors with stronger abnormal signals.
* Yaki ship research is improved if you have infamy.
* Terran ships can be researched only in sectors with Terran Memory.
* You can use your Data Scanner to scan your own ships whose blueprints you have not yet unlocked.
--- Fleet Combat Tips ---

* If you cannot catch someone, you cannot kill them. Speed kills. For example, the Split have the fastest ships, but they are somewhat weak in defenses. Used properly, they can be deadly. Each faction has its own particular advantages to learn and exploit.
* Escort your large capital ships with some M6s. These provide good anti-fighter defense and they can hold up in a heavy fight.

* Create fast raiding fleets of M3s. In the Fleet Settings screen, set them to attack only enemy freighters and patrol an enemy faction's space. They will quickly decimate enemy haulers while running from other fights. This can devastate the economy of an opponent.

* Missiles in Renegades have greatly enhanced damage. They are expensive but deal more damage than in any prior versions of X3 mods. M7Ms are very effective long-range anti-capital forces, and M8s can be devastating against fighters.

* Grouping your forces is essential to surviving large engagements. Streaming in your attack ships one by one is the best way to lose them. When invading a sector, consider first sending in one or two fast fighters and directing them to the far side of the target sector. When the defenses move far from your gate to engage those fighters, stream in your large ships.

* For large capital ship engagements in-sector, use fast, nimble fighters to draw fire from enemy capital ships and away from your capital ships. These force the enemy to waste their high-damage weapons on nimble, hard-to-hit ships.
* Be sure to set up a Supplier in the Fleet Settings screen to automatically restore your missile reserves.
* Moving capital ships through gates is vastly slower with the player in-sector. If you need to get them through a gate fast, be somewhere else.
--- Logistics Tips ---

* In sectors that don't have a Jump Beacon, use only local Agents to import from and export to local factories, then set other Agents to move full loads between other Outposts. This maximizes the inter-sector loads you carry and is the key to efficiency.
* In general, an Agent can support up to 3-4 factories. For example, sectors with 15 factories may need 3-4 Agents.
* A Courier is more efficient than an Agent when transferring multiple wares between Outposts.

* Outpost Traders are used for buying materials from NPCs or selling excess items to NPCs. When neither is needed, they start trading between NPCs for pure profit, so they can be a huge source of income over time. Any successful trade with an NPC improves your reputation with its faction.
* If you can afford the maintenance costs, research a fast TS-class ship to use as your Agents. The faster resources are moved around your empire, the smoother it will run.
* If you find your Agents doing nothing most of the time, assign them to do something else. Optimize the use of your Agents to keep costs down.

* Your logistics ships will need maintenance once in a while. Be sure to review your Maintenance screen in your Personal Console and occasionally send them for inspection. Otherwise their maintenance will be very high.
--- General Tips ---
* Use Private Corp. ships to fill gaps in your fleet. They are flexible, but specialized faction ships perform better in combat.
* For example, the Truelight Seeker excels at repairs but is less effective in combat.
* The Aran serves as a mobile base, repairing ships 4x faster than standard carriers, but cannot fight.
* Do not undervalue mining ships. While mining ore and silicon, they also collect colored crystals which are used for ship upgrades and as commodities at trade stations.

* On harder difficulties and fighting far from home, consider loading a cheap factory and a Jump Beacon on one of your capital ships, assuming you have one with the necessary cargo space.

* Generally, a faction must share a border with you in order to declare war on you. Higher difficulties increase the chance of going to war.

* Renegade ships move faster when they start fleeing to a station.

* All ships you own consume supply. Monitor your supply usage carefully: exceeding capacity will not only increase ship construction and maintenance costs but also cause other factions to increase their vigilance.
--- Fleet Settings Screen Tips ---

* If you want your fleets to focus their fire on one target at a time, set their scanning range to 0 km, and set "Followers engage commander's target" to YES. It can be less efficient, but you will lose fewer ships.

* You can assign an automated Missile Supplier that will top up all your ships in the field. Upgrade a TS hauler with a Transporter Device and position it out in space. In the Fleet Settings screen, select "Supplier:" and choose this hauler.

* A Supplier will retrieve missiles from its homebase or request that its homebase build more as needed. It automatically restocks your ships. Set your ship restock amounts at the bottom of the "Advanced/Weapons..." menu for that ship.
* This screen shows the slowest ship in the fleet. This is important because a fleet travels at the pace of its slowest member.
* For fast raiding fleets composed of fighters, it is useful to select the option to "Ignore Big and Huge Ships".
* Fleets can automatically reinforce themselves by setting the "Build Followers" menu. This is limited to only one type of ship, but it can be useful for homogeneous fleets.
--- Hacking Tips ---

* Oxygen and accounting hacks take the longest to complete.
* The "Hacking Station" perk is required to convert a research station into a hacking station.
* Good Hacking Station locations cover a lot of nearby sectors. Place them as close to the targets as possible.

--- Boarding Tips ---

* In general, new marines need to go through at least one deck's worth of time in order to reinforce your surviving marines. They need more time the farther you are from your target when you launch Boarding Pods.
* Boarding can net you a lot of resources, but it is generally frowned upon and also has its own set of risks.
* Boarding abandoned ships results in significantly fewer losses than boarding manned ships.
* Shield Hack and EMP can be used as alternatives to keep your target's shields down.
* Boarding a ship yields up to the first 25% of a ship blueprint and some valuables.
* Roaming Renegade ships are most valuable when captured intentionally rather than destroyed.

--- Storyline and OCV Tips ---
* As you progress through the main plot, you can choose to continue helping Phanon or to progress through the Synthetic Dawn Plot and join the OCV. Each route has its advantages.
* The main plot normally starts when you have established an empire, but the alternate route can be started as soon as you place your first Outpost.
